description:
The phrase '.expect("derive(Serialize) on plain data is infallible")' appears in event.rs (3x), participant_identity.rs (2x), calendar.rs (2x), helpers.rs (1x) — 8 times in this crate alone. Workspace-wide it appears in 13 files across jmap-calendars-server and jmap-mail-server (5x in email.rs, 4x in memory.rs, 3x in submission.rs and mailbox.rs, etc.) — roughly 30 occurrences.

Each site is the same pattern:
  serde_json::to_value(&created_obj).expect("derive(Serialize) on plain data is infallible")

This is a documented invariant ('plain data + derive(Serialize) cannot fail') with an explanatory message, so the .expect() itself is defensible per workspace AGENTS.md (which forbids unexplained .unwrap()/.expect()). The problem is the duplication: 30 copies of the same explanation in the same crate-family is noise, and a future contributor who changes the invariant (adds a custom Serialize impl, adds a non-stringifiable field) has to track down every site.

Idiomatic fix: add to crate::helpers (and the canonical sibling crate::helpers in jmap-mail-server) a small inline helper:
    pub(crate) fn to_jmap_value<T: Serialize>(obj: &T) -> Value {
        serde_json::to_value(obj).expect("derive(Serialize) on plain data is infallible")
    }

Every call site becomes 'to_jmap_value(&created_obj)' — single source of truth for the invariant, single .expect() site to audit if the invariant ever changes. set_error_value (helpers.rs:107) already follows exactly this shape for SetError; the broader pattern just needs the same treatment.

Per the workspace canonical-template rule (AGENTS.md 'Canonical Templates'): fix the canonical jmap-mail-server first, then propagate to all 7 extension-server siblings in the same pass.
title: Repeated .expect("derive(Serialize) on plain data is infallible") at every /set call site — should be a helper
